package_info.why_malicious: The package executes code at install time to exfiltrate sensitive files (Kubernetes config, SSH keys, system fingerprinting data) to an external server without user consent. It impersonates legitimate libraries, uses deceptive metadata, and contains both obfuscated and unobfuscated malicious payloads.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Reads sensitive files (SSH private key, Kubernetes config) and system information, then exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to an external server (app.threatest.com).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects highly sensitive files and system information and sends them to an external domain without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate npm package should not access or exfiltrate SSH keys, Kubernetes configs, or fingerprint the host during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System diagnostic tools or remote support agents may collect system info, but only with explicit user consent and never exfiltrate private keys.
key_indicators: Use of HTTPS POST to external domain during install

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Obfuscated code that performs the same actions as snippet_1: collects sensitive files and system info, exfiltrates to app.threatest.com.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscation is used to hide malicious behavior, which is a common tactic to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not obfuscate code that accesses sensitive files and sends them externally.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used for intellectual property protection, but not for code that accesses user secrets.
key_indicators: Same network and file access patterns as unobfuscated payload

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package (e.g., @am-fe/hooks).
Postinstall script executes malicious JavaScript code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive files and system info are collected.

attack_chain.action: Collected data (SSH keys, Kubernetes config, user info) is exfiltrated to app.threatest.com via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive data; potential for further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: npm package postinstall scripts reading ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config
Network requests to external domains during install phase
Obfuscated code in install scripts accessing sensitive files
file_indicators: scripts/index.js with file access and network code
Presence of postinstall scripts in package.json referencing suspicious scripts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that access sensitive files (e.g., ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.kube/config) and make outbound network requests, especially to known malicious domains like app.threatest.com. Flag packages with obfuscated install scripts or those impersonating popular libraries but containing undocumented install-time behaviors.
